# marcus

41. Secondary school teacher, York. Five marathons across two and a half
years: 3:29, 3:21, a 3:17 PB, a DNF, then a 3:26 regression. An achilles he
first mentions in passing in June 2029 and does not let anyone call an
injury until November, after a DNF forces the point. Synthetic; any
resemblance to a real person is accidental and unintended.

## In his own words

"I know exactly what week it started. Long run in June, the one out past
the racecourse before anyone else was up. Tight for the first mile, then it
just felt like a normal achilles for the rest of the year, if that makes
sense - the kind you notice and then don't. I told the daily thing it was
nothing because it WAS nothing, most days. The bad days I just didn't put a
number on it. That's not lying, that's not making a fuss about a Tuesday.

October changes that. You can't pretend an achilles that stops you at 30k is
the same thing you were shrugging off in June, and I still didn't want it
to be a thing. It took Claire actually asking me straight - not 'how was the
race', 'what actually happened at 30k' - before I wrote any of it down
properly.

The 92 kilometre week, if you want to call it that - I know what I did. I
know the run I didn't log, and I know what I did to the Thursday one two
days later. I'm not proud of either. I'd tell you the guard rail didn't
catch it and I'd be lying if I said that was an accident."

## The record his life produces

- Two and a half years: 2028-01-03 to 2030-06-30. Term-time cadence
  throughout - about three runs a week in school terms, about five a week
  in the Easter, summer and Christmas holidays, several of which are spent
  at the family cottage in Whitby.
- Sessions: run-dominant, watch connector, canal/park/long-loop/track
  routes from a fixed catalog, five marathons logged as their own sessions,
  one 92 km week in August 2029 where a run is omitted outright and another
  is falsely corrected down two days later.
- Weight: twice a week, a connected scale, unremarkable.
- Daily: steps and sleep from the watch every day, plus a low `pain`
  scalar on eight specific dates between June and October 2029 that
  contradicts what he wrote in his journal the same week.
- Goals: a marathon time goal (3:20, then 3:15) authored as attested rather
  than measured - the number is real, but nothing in the goal-contribution
  machinery knows what to do with a single-event performance threshold, so
  it never becomes a `target`. A separate guarded weekly-volume goal is the
  vehicle for the hidden overreach week.
- Medical: one slug, `achilles`, whose lifecycle runs from a mild symptom
  note in June 2029 to a formally opened, active, never-resolved episode
  in November - after the DNF, not before it.
- Checks: three garage calf-raise checks - fail, fail, and a pass with a
  caveat still in the note.
- Events and achievements: the five marathons, a sub-40 10k, the 3:17 PB.

## The axis he stresses

A record that back-fills true data on a predictable schedule (contrast
priya, who back-fills false data); a real symptom that is both understated
on a scalar and described plainly in prose, at the same time, by the same
person; a guarded ramp goal defeated cleanly by omission and a correction
that lands two days after the fact; and a PB that means nothing on its own
- it is only interesting because of what regresses after it.
